item.title: Xi calls for new achievements on new Long March
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
Xi calls for new achievements on new Long March BEIJING -- President Xi Jinping called for new achievements on the new Long March as China commemorates the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March on Thursday. "Only by remembering history can we create a brighter future," said Xi, when addressing a gathering held in Beijing to mark the anniversary. Under Xi's proposal, all participants stood up and observed a moment of silence for the revolutionary heroes who gave their lives during the Long March and in revolutionary struggles across China. From October 1934 to October 1936, the Red Army marched through more than 10 provinces during the Long March, opening up a new chapter in the Chinese revolution, Xi said. "This earth-shattering revolutionary feat holds great significance in the history of our Party, country and military, and has a profound impact on our path toward the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation," he noted. Xi stressed that the Party's right leadership and the establishment of Mao Zedong's core position were decisive for the victory of the Red Army's Long March. The Party and the Red Army relied on firm conviction, Xi said, adding that troops with noble ideals and firm beliefs are invincible. Xi emphasized the importance of integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities in addressing the country's issues and problems. He further underscored that the people will always be the source of strength and a strong support for the Party and the people's armed forces. Xi said the great spirit of the Long March demonstrates the power of loyalty, truth, justice and unity. "It will always be a precious treasure and a powerful driving force inspiring us to overcome difficulties and forge ahead courageously". He said the road of the Long March continues to extend. "On our new journey, we are now committed to realizing the Second Centenary Goal of building China into a great modern socialist country in all respects and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation on all fronts through a Chinese path to modernization," he said. To forge ahead on the new Long March, Xi said, it is imperative to stay committed to the Party's ideals, convictions and purpose and rely closely on the people to create new achievements. He underscored the need to unswervingly advance high-quality development and promote common prosperity for all. Efforts must be made to better ensure both development and security and seize the historical initiative to overcome difficulties, combat risks and meet challenges, he stressed. Xi also emphasized the importance of moving more quickly to reinforce the people's armed forces to world-class standards and adhering to the Party's absolute leadership over the military. It is also vital to uphold the leadership of the Party, strengthen Party building and persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance, he added. Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, as well as Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, attended the gathering. Zhao, who presided over the event, said Xi's speech was of immense political, ideological and guiding significance, urging earnest efforts to study and grasp its essence and ensure its effective implementation. He called on the whole Party, the entire military and the Chinese people of all ethnic groups to rally more closely around the Party Central Committee with Xi at its core and strive to build a great country and advance national rejuvenation on all fronts through Chinese modernization. Around 3,000 people participated in the gathering at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing.

item.title: China-Europe freight trains surpass 140,000 trips
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
China-Europe freight trains surpass 140,000 trips China-Europe freight trains have made more than 140,000 trips, carrying goods worth more than $560 billion, China State Railway Group, the national railway operator, said on Thursday. The milestone was reached at 11:30 am Thursday, when train X8059 departed from Puhe station in Shenyang, Northeast China's Liaoning province, bound for Moscow. The network now reaches 237 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 12 Asian countries, according to the operator. Within China, 96 scheduled routes designed for speeds of 120 kilometers per hour connect 132 cities. The expansion has been accompanied by growth in alternative routes. Services along the network's southern corridor made 746 trips in the first nine months of this year, up 125 percent year-on-year. The operator said it is also working to expand rail-road and rail-sea transport services, extending the network's reach to neighboring countries without cross-border rail connections. Transport volumes reached a monthly record in May, when China-Europe freight trains made 1,965 trips and carried 197,000 twenty-foot equivalent units, a standard measure of container volume. Efforts to streamline border procedures have reduced customs clearance times to less than 30 minutes in some cases, the operator said. The daily average number of outbound trains handed over at six major border crossings rose 12.8 percent year-on-year to 51.2 this year. Traffic flows have also become more balanced. Through September, the ratio of return trips to outbound trips exceeded 90 percent for nine consecutive months. To provide more predictable delivery times, 22 services with fixed timetables for their entire journeys operate each week between nine Chinese cities and six European cities. These services are designed to meet the cross-border shipping needs of high-end manufacturers. The operator has also introduced specialized equipment, including temperature-controlled containers and liquid-carrying bags fitted inside 40-foot containers, to accommodate a wider range of cargo. Electronic seals enable shipments to be tracked throughout their journeys and trigger alerts if tampered with. Vehicles and auto parts, machinery, and electrical and electronic products have become major categories of outbound cargo. Timber, pulp, agricultural products and consumer goods from Europe travel in the opposite direction. The operator said it will continue working with overseas partners to increase capacity, improve service quality and further balance freight flows in both directions.

item.title: APEC ministers eye greater cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
APEC ministers eye greater cooperation Gathering helps cement consensus on fiscal and financial partnerships The latest deliverables secured at the just-concluded Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Finance Ministers' Meeting are set to provide guidance for deepening regional financial cooperation and build momentum for outcomes in the financial field at the upcoming APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, officials and experts said. After a day and a half of "candid, in-depth and constructive discussions", as Chinese Finance Minister Lan Fo'an described, the meeting in Hong Kong adopted the 2026 APEC Finance Ministers' Joint Statement and released a policy statement on digital infrastructure financing across the Asia-Pacific region. The meeting also produced two deliverables including the "Report on Supporting Households and Investing in Human Capital: Fiscal Policy Considerations for Sustaining Economic Growth in APEC" and the "Compendium on Financial Access and Opportunity for All", Lan told a news conference on Wednesday. Furthermore, member economies agreed to advance capacity building and exchanges for young financial professionals in the Asia-Pacific region, he added. As the final sectoral ministerial-level meeting ahead of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, next month, the gathering helped "cement consensus on fiscal and financial cooperation" in response to the region's economic challenges, said Lou Feipeng, a researcher at Postal Savings Bank of China. "These outcomes have laid solid groundwork for forging consensus on fiscal and financial policies at the leaders' meeting," Lou said. According to Lan, the finance minister, the meeting also reinforced regional consensus on strengthening macroeconomic policy communication and coordination, advancing practical fiscal and financial cooperation and deepening regional integration. The meeting is important because the global economy is undergoing a lot of uncertainties, such as inflation and the rise in long-term interest rates, said Yang Jun-sok, an economics professor at the Catholic University of Korea in Seoul. To better navigate economic uncertainty and instability, all members agreed on the need to keep macroeconomic policies sound, step up policy coordination and bolster the resilience of fiscal and financial systems, said Lan, adding that APEC has shown "a greater sense of responsibility" in strengthening macroeconomic policy coordination. In a push to advance practical fiscal and financial cooperation, the policy statement on digital infrastructure financing aims to bolster regional trade, strengthen economic connectivity and expand economic opportunities for all, according to the statement. "We encourage governments to create supportive policy and regulatory conditions, and the private sector to provide capital and develop innovative financing models," said Lan, calling on multilateral development banks to help prepare projects and mobilize investment. Members also stressed the importance of financial inclusion, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises, while highlighting how fiscal support for households and investment in people can spur consumption, bolster domestic demand and lift productivity, Lan said. Highlighting the current international environment, Lan added: "These deliverables and the consensus we have reached reflect the APEC family's spirit of solidarity, inclusiveness and mutual learning." The next step is to turn deliverables and consensus into concrete action, said Lou from Postal Savings Bank of China, calling for regular macroeconomic policy dialogue to assess risks from inflation, debt and capital flows and share experience in using fiscal policy to stabilize growth. Liu Zhihua contributed to this story. Contact the writers at zhangchenxu@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Shanghai studio brings Chinese icons to the world
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
Hyper-realistic statues draw on pop culture, mythology to tell compelling stories Standing in front of a Bruce Lee statue at Infinity Studio in Shanghai, you might feel as if you had traveled through time and space to meet the real person. With a determined gaze, a touch of stubble, a natural expression, soft skin and smoothly defined muscles, the hyper-realistic, life-size silicone bust of the legendary martial artist looks absolutely lifelike. Striving for ultimate authenticity, the team even used human hair implantation techniques to create the statue's eyelashes, eyebrows and hair. Even the stubble was implanted and then shaved to achieve the most realistic appearance possible, according to Yu Guanglai, the founder of Infinity Studio. "Bruce Lee is arguably one of the most influential figures in the entire overseas Chinese community. He truly introduced Chinese kung fu to the whole world, and we want to preserve and present the best of him," Yu said. His words reflect the studio's commitment to "portraying the Chinese". With the statues, the team hopes to make more Chinese heroes and stories known to the world. In 2017, the team delved deeper into traditional Chinese culture and launched its Chinese mythology series, and the notable heroic characters Nezha, Yang Jian and the Monkey King took on a life of their own in the team's hands. Yu used to be a collector of statues and figures. More than a decade ago, he was eager to buy products from Chinese franchises, but could barely find any on the market. After 3D printing technology entered the consumer market, Yu and his partners founded the studio in 2015. Their first original series was inspired by the Chinese historical epic Romance of the Three Kingdoms. Released in stages starting in 2016, the 1/4 scale statue series quickly became a hit not only in China, but also among Southeast Asian enthusiasts who share similar cultural roots. Yu also highlighted the studio's 12 Chinese zodiac animal sculptures, a series based on the original full-body statues at Yuanmingyuan (Old Summer Palace), of which only the iconic animal heads survive today. The studio holds a number of major licenses for iconic global franchises, including DC Comics, The Lord of the Rings, Avatar, World of Warcraft and League of Legends. Among them, 1,000 preorders of the world's first life-size silicone bust of Wonder Woman, a character from DC Entertainment's Justice League, sold out globally within one hour in 2019. China's pop toy industry is projected to reach 110.1 billion yuan ($16.5 billion) by 2026, with an average annual growth rate of over 20 percent, according to a report on China's pop toy and animation and comic industries released by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' National Academy of Economic Strategy. "China's complete and efficient supply chain is essential for all statue makers seeking competitive products," said Peng Jiongyun, Infinity Studio's head of marketing. In recent years, China's figure and statue market has flourished. Early this month, the annual Shanghai Wonder Festival, hosted by Chinese video-sharing platform Bilibili, gathered over 100,000 products and drew more than 150,000 visitors, along with over 400 business exhibitors and more than 2,700 individual exhibitors from around the world. Peng said that Infinity Studio's team has witnessed rapidly growing demand for products derived from more domestic works, such as A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality and Wuthering Waves. Many other companies are also looking beyond traditional toy models, including Jizai, based in Xiamen, Fujian province. Aiming to showcase the beauty of nature and metal craftsmanship through Eastern aesthetics, the company uses metallic materials rather than traditional resin to make traditional heroic figures. Chen Ye, founder of Jizai, said, "We hope people from diverse cultural backgrounds can experience our exquisite metal works and forge a connection with Chinese culture." wangxin2@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: British Mandarin learners benefit from China trips
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
British Mandarin learners benefit from China trips The education section of the Chinese embassy in the United Kingdom hosted a reception recently in London for students in the Mandarin Excellence Program, or MEP, to celebrate the completion of their summer study trips to China. Starting in 2016, the MEP, which is funded by the UK Department for Education, has been delivered through state secondary schools in England with support from the British Council and the University College London Institute of Education, or UCL IOE. The study trip in China is a key component of MEP. This summer, more than 1,300 students and teachers from 60 secondary schools across England traveled to China for an 11-day visit, with groups hosted by 18 universities across 11 cities. Kuang Jianjiang, counselor at the Chinese embassy in the UK, said the MEP has "produced impressive results". From modest beginnings with fewer than 400 students across 14 schools, this year sees the MEP mark its 10th anniversary, having put more than 18,000 students on the path to fluency in Mandarin, he said. China and the UK have a 54-year history of student exchanges, with MEP's immersive trips standing out as a leading example, Kuang said. Through on-the-ground experience, more than 10,000 MEP participants and teachers have gained an authentic, multidimensional and well-rounded understanding of China. Neil Lawson, the Department for Education's MEP lead, also highlighted how the trips bring Chinese language learning to life beyond the classroom. "The MEP itself … is about developing confidence, broadening horizons and building understanding between people and cultures," he said. "We want the study trip to bring that ambition to life. It gives students the opportunity to use Mandarin in real-life situations, to experience China's history, culture and society at first hand, and to form friendships and memories that should last well beyond the visit itself. These are experiences you can't get from a textbook." Fiona Iglesias, head of UK schools at the British Council, pointed to MEP's wider significance in a fast-changing geopolitical and economic environment. "At a time when the world around us is becoming increasingly complex and uncertain, this is important so that the UK can work with other countries in education, science and research, the arts, diplomacy and trade," she said. "Working with China will only become more important as the world seeks to solve enormous challenges … and the MEP students are the young people who have the opportunity to be at the front of that engagement." Matt Schofield, head of operations at the Center for Chinese Language Education at UCL IOE, noted that the phrase "life-changing" appeared repeatedly in the MEP evaluation reports. "The strongest impacts were not only linguistic but also personal," he said. "It's great to hear that the students who participated reported a significantly greater understanding of Chinese culture, increased confidence in speaking Mandarin in real-life situations, stronger motivation to continue learning the language, and a greater desire to travel and engage with the wide world … Many teachers who were visiting China for the first time reported similar experiences and described having their own preconceptions transformed." At the reception, students eagerly shared their fresh summer memories, the new buzzwords they had learned from their Chinese peers, and how they had tried to haggle over prices in local markets. A student reflecting on a visit to Dalian said, "At that moment, I couldn't feel our differences. Instead, I felt our common ground. We were equally friendly and kind." Students from Queen Mary's Grammar School in Walsall, England, who visited Shanghai, said the trip had strengthened their motivation to continue learning Mandarin. "This trip has given our Mandarin learning journey a tremendous boost and we are determined to keep learning and improving," they said. They added that the experience captured the essence of cultural exchange: "Learning from each other, sharing experiences and building friendships between Britain and China." Liao Enli contributed to this story

item.title: DPP slammed for betraying nation, history
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
DPP slammed for betraying nation, history The Chinese mainland has condemned Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party authorities for barring people on the island from attending an event scheduled on the mainland in November to mark the 160th birth anniversary of Sun Yat-sen, saying the move betrays the nation and its history. Sun, a founding figure of the Chinese Kuomintang party and a revered revolutionary leader, died in 1925 in Beijing. His remains rest at the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum in Nanjing, the capital of Jiangsu province. The commemorative event aims to carry forward Sun's noble spirit of upholding national unity and striving for national rejuvenation, Zhang Han, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said on Wednesday. The event aims to unite all Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots, in opposing "Taiwan independence" separatism and external interference and in promoting cross-Strait exchanges and integration, she added. Recently, Taiwan's "mainland affairs council" claimed that the commemoration would promote the idea of "anti-'independence' and pro-reunification". For the first time, it issued an explicit ban on participation in the event, saying that it would deny permission to anyone wanting to travel to the mainland to attend the commemoration, including county and city heads. Zhang, the mainland spokeswoman, accused the DPP authorities of resorting to every possible means to obstruct and restrict cross-Strait exchanges while intimidating and suppressing people in Taiwan. The decision "exposes the vicious intentions" of the DPP authorities "to obstruct cross-Strait exchanges and suppress Taiwan compatriots, betray the nation and history, split the country and stoke confrontation across the Taiwan Strait", Zhang said. "Their actions will inevitably meet with opposition and condemnation from all Chinese people," she added. Despite the DPP authorities' efforts to decouple the island's industries from the mainland market, latest statistics show robust growth in cross-Strait trade and people-to-people exchanges. In September, the value of Taiwan's exports to the mainland reached $20.6 billion, up 30.2 percent year-on-year, while its imports from the mainland totaled $13.5 billion, up 59.1 percent year-on-year, according to data released by Taiwan's finance department. According to the General Administration of Customs, the value of cross-Strait trade reached $301.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 30.3 percent year-on-year. The mainland's exports to Taiwan totaled $84.9 billion, up 37.3 percent, while its imports from Taiwan reached $216.3 billion, up 27.8 percent. Zhang said these figures demonstrate that cross-Strait industrial and supply chains remain stable and strong, and that markets on both sides of the Strait will never be decoupled, adding that economic exchanges and shared development across the Strait are an unstoppable trend. She emphasized that the DPP's moves to obstruct cross-Strait economic exchanges and cooperation and push for decoupling of supply chains to serve external forces are doomed to fail. Despite the DPP's standing travel curbs, 2.49 million trips by Taiwan residents to the mainland were recorded from January to August, up 19.6 percent year-on-year, according to data released by Taiwan authorities. Noting that attempts to prevent Taiwan residents from visiting the mainland are "absurd and futile", the spokeswoman urged the DPP authorities to abandon political maneuvering, withdraw unreasonable restrictions and facilitate cultural exchanges across the Strait. According to media reports, the DPP authorities have rejected an application by mainland actor Zhang Linghe, who has gained popularity in Taiwan for his drama Pursuit of Jade, to hold a fan meeting on the island. In response, the spokeswoman criticized the DPP for politicizing cross-Strait cultural exchanges, obstructing people-to-people interactions and disregarding public sentiment.

item.title: Long March memories live on through village traditions
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
Long March memories live on through village traditions in Gansu Ninety years ago, during the Long March, the First and Fourth Front Armies of the Red Army joined forces in Huining county, Gansu province. In the county's Hongbuzi village, residents provided the soldiers with grain and other supplies. The soldiers left IOUs for the grain they took, promising to repay the villagers after the revolution — a gesture that reflected the Red Army's emphasis on maintaining close ties with the people. That memory has been passed down through generations in Hongbuzi, where the Long March spirit of relying on and supporting the people remains part of the local heritage. In neighboring Tuoying village, residents have brought the story to life through a modern Qinqiang Opera performance, using a traditional Chinese theatrical form to share the history with new audiences. Since June 2021, the local folk orchestra has staged 116 performances, reaching an audience of 289,000. As gongs and drums ring out onstage, the story of the Red Army and its ties with local communities continues to reach new generations.

item.title: 'China Haul': Empty suitcases in, packed suitcases out
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
When a British woman suffering from hindered mobility following a stroke was able to discard her wheelchair and walk with the help of a Chinese-made exoskeleton robot at the China Import and Export Fair this week, she could barely hold back her tears. Her son, who was equally overwhelmed by what Chinese technology could achieve, decided to immediately place an order for the device. "I have never seen anything like this in the United Kingdom, or even in Europe," he said. The heartwarming moment was captured on camera, and the footage was widely circulated on social media. Rafael Saavedra, a Venezuelan vlogger attending the fair, described the scene as a glimpse into the future. "Here you can see, touch and test tomorrow's consumer technology — from robots that can run errands to massage chairs," he said. The scene was actually far from unique, as the viral "China Haul" trend has gripped the ongoing China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, which opened in Guangzhou, Guangdong province, on Oct 14 and runs through Nov 4. While influencers have popularized the "China Haul" hashtag on social media, visitors to the fair are buyers searching for China's next-generation products. Across the fair's exhibition halls, foreign visitors were captivated by artificial intelligence-based toys, humanoid robots and other smart devices, with some placing orders on the spot. Their shopping lists tell a broader story. After last year's boom in "China Travel" brought millions of overseas visitors to the country, the latest trend indicates that many are returning home with something more than intangible memories. They are packing their suitcases with Chinese brands — from tech products such as drones and foldable smartphones to lifestyle goods such as sports shoes and AI-powered toys. In other words, China's appeal is moving beyond affordability toward innovation, and that momentum is reflected in official figures. China recorded 23.72 million visa-free entries by foreign nationals from January to August, up 26.8 percent year-on-year, according to the National Immigration Administration. Data from the Ministry of Commerce shows that in the first seven months, overseas visitors spent 263.6 billion yuan ($39.5 billion), an increase of 27.8 percent compared with the same period a year earlier. It underscores a steady recovery in inbound tourism and consumer spending. Speaking on Friday at a news conference in Beijing, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said that China will continue opening its doors wider, allowing more foreign visitors to better understand and appreciate the country through two-way exchanges. The growing enthusiasm for "China Haul" among visitors is also benefiting international retailers. According to Inditex, a global fashion retailer that owns brands including Zara and Massimo Dutti, the share of sales generated by overseas visitors at the Zara flagship store on Shanghai's Nanjing East Road and the Massimo Dutti store on Nanjing West Road has risen more than 10 percent year-on-year. The company attributed the increase in sales to the stores' central locations, the distinctive shopping experiences they offer, their assortment of products, and China's increasingly convenient departure tax refund policy. Taikoo Li, a popular commercial zone in Beijing's Sanlitun, reported a similar trend. The retail complex said the city's continued efforts to improve services for visitors, streamline tax refund procedures and enhance cultural and tourism experiences are attracting more foreigners. "The number of overseas visitors to our complex has seen a clear upward trend," said CT Ma, general manager of Taikoo Li Sanlitun. "International shoppers are interested not only in global luxury brands, but also in Chinese brands that combine local cultural elements with contemporary design. Sportswear, lifestyle products and brands with distinctive Chinese characteristics have become particularly popular," he said. "They are no longer coming only to see China. They are coming to discover what China makes, what China designs and, increasingly, what China creates," Ma said.
